# Sentinel-as-opt-out lets users adopt generated files without fighting the generator
**Source**: manual
**Date**: 2026-04-07
When a tool generates files into a user-editable location (e.g. `.claude/rules/typescript.md`), the obvious problem is: what happens when the user edits one? Two common designs:

1. **Always regenerate** — destroys user edits, painful on every update.
2. **Never regenerate if file exists** — bugfixes in shipped templates never reach existing projects.

Better: embed a canonical sentinel comment as the first non-frontmatter line. On regeneration, check for the sentinel; if present → safe to overwrite (file is still "owned by rulebook"); if absent → user has adopted the file, preserve it verbatim.

Concrete implementation in `src/core/rules-generator.ts`:
- Sentinel: `<!-- Generated by @hivehub/rulebook v5.3.0 — delete this comment to prevent regeneration on rulebook update -->`
- Placed immediately after the `---` frontmatter block (inside markdown, invisible in rendered output, trivially greppable)
- `hasGeneratedSentinel(content)` is a one-line `content.includes(SENTINEL)` check

Why this works:
- Users who want rulebook to keep the rule fresh → leave the sentinel, edit elsewhere
- Users who want to own the rule → delete the sentinel line, keep or rewrite everything
- No config flag, no database, no external state — the file itself declares its ownership
- Transparent: `grep -l "Generated by @hivehub/rulebook" .claude/rules/` lists all rulebook-owned files

Pattern used in: `src/core/rules-generator.ts`. Tested in `tests/rules-generator.test.ts` ("preserves user-authored rule files" and "overwrites previously generated rule files").
